title: roboRIO
summary: Status lights, unrecoverable errors, microSD card, imaging, USB and Ethernet reachability.

start.question: Look at the roboRIO lights. What do you see?
start.help: Lights from left: Power, Status, Radio (unused), Comm, Mode, RSL.

options.label: Comm light off, DS cannot see the robot
Comm green but robot will not move

no-power.title: roboRIO has no power
steps: Confirm the robot main breaker is on and the PDH or PDP shows a status light.
Tug the RIO power Weidmuller plug. Pull the wires, strip fresh copper, push them back in until they lock.
Check the RIO channel on the PDH or PDP. Reseat the fuse or breaker. A red channel LED means no output.
Measure 12 V at the RIO plug. 12 V with no lights means the RIO is dead.

steps.text: Is the RIO still dark with 12 V at the plug?
steps.yes: Swap the roboRIO, image it, set the team number.

power-color.question: Is the Power light amber or red?

brownout.title: Amber Power light: brownout protection tripped
steps: Read the battery voltage in the DS. Under 12.3 V at rest means a weak battery. Swap it for a fully charged one.
Check the DS log for dips below 6.8 V when motors start. That is a brownout. Lower motor supply current limits, drive first.
Wiggle the battery connector and main breaker lugs. Try to rotate each lug. Tighten any that turns.
Put the RIO power wires on their own PDH or PDP channel, not shared with the radio or a motor.

steps.text: Does the Power light still show amber?
steps.yes: Look at the DS log with the team for the limits.

rail-short.title: Red Power light: short on a user rail
steps: Power off. Unplug everything from the RIO DIO, PWM, analog, and the 5 V and 6 V rails.
Power on with nothing connected. Green now means plug devices back one at a time to find the short.
Look for a stray wire strand or a metal chip touching the RIO pins. Clean it out.
Check any sensor cable with a crushed or pinched jacket.

steps.text: Is the Power light still red with nothing plugged in?

which-rio.question: Which roboRIO is it?
which-rio.help: roboRIO 2 has a microSD card slot on the side and a 2.0 label. roboRIO 1 has no card slot.

rio2-status.question: How is the Status light blinking?

options.label: Flashing all the time, never pauses
Groups of 2, 3, or 4 flashes, then a pause
Stays on solid after a minute

rio1-status.question: How is the Status light blinking?

options.label: Stays on solid after a minute

rio2-unrecoverable.title: roboRIO 2 unrecoverable error: continuous flashing
steps: On a roboRIO 2 a Status light that flashes without pausing means it cannot boot from the microSD card.
Power off. Pull the microSD card. Look in the slot for metal chips or debris. Blow it out. Reseat the card until it clicks.
Power on and wait 60 seconds.

steps.text: Is the Status light still flashing?

steps: Reimage the card on a laptop with balenaEtcher or Raspberry Pi Imager, then set the team number with the Imaging Tool and redeploy the robot code.

steps.text: Is it still flashing after a reimage?
steps.yes: Try a fresh microSD card, or swap the roboRIO.

links.label: NI forum: RIO 2 stuck in unrecoverable error

rio1-unrecoverable.title: roboRIO 1 unrecoverable error: 4 flashes then a pause
steps: On a roboRIO 1, 4 flashes then a pause means the software crashed twice without a reboot.
Press the reset button once. Wait 60 seconds.

steps.text: Is it still 4 flashes then a pause?

steps: Hold reset at least 5 seconds to boot into Safe Mode. Connect by USB and reimage with the Imaging Tool, Format Target.
Set the team number and redeploy the robot code.
Check the RIO power wiring. A loose Weidmuller on the RIO plug can crash it at power on.

steps.text: Does it still crash or refuse to image?

blink-codes.title: Status blink codes: 2, 3, or 4 flashes
steps: 2 flashes: software error. Reimage the roboRIO.
3 flashes: Safe Mode. Press reset once. Reimage if it comes back in Safe Mode.
4 flashes on a roboRIO 2: software crashed twice. Reboot. Reimage if it repeats.
Before reimaging a roboRIO 2, reseat the microSD card and check the slot for debris.

steps.text: Does the Status light still blink a code?
steps.yes: Reimage, set the team number, and redeploy.

reach.question: Can the laptop reach the RIO at all?
reach.help: Test over USB first. Plug a USB A to B cable into the RIO and open http://172.22.11.2/ in a browser.

options.label: Yes over USB, no over Ethernet
Not tested yet, only tried the network

reach-network.title: Check the network path to the RIO
steps: From the DS laptop run ping 10.TE.AM.2 (team 1234 is 10.12.34.2). A reply means the network is fine and the DS setup is the problem.
No reply: check the RIO Ethernet cable is in the radio RIO port and both ends show link lights.
Turn off Wi-Fi and disable every adapter except the one connected to the radio. Set that adapter to DHCP.
Turn off the Windows firewall. Check the Robot Radio and Robot ping lights in the DS Diagnostics tab.

steps.text: Does the radio ping but the RIO does not?
steps.yes: Plug into the RIO by USB and test again.

ethernet-dead.title: RIO works over USB but not Ethernet
steps: On the RIO web page over USB, check the Ethernet interface has an address. Blank means no link.
Swap the Ethernet cable. Prove the cable and radio on another port, then move it back to the RIO port.
Look at the RIO port for bent pins or a broken latch tab on the plug.
Plug a USB Ethernet adapter into the RIO USB A port and run the radio cable to it. The RIO picks it up as a second interface. This has got a robot through an event with a dead port.

steps.text: Is the RIO Ethernet port still dead?
steps.yes: Swap the roboRIO and contact NI for a repair.

links.label: NI KB: Ethernet port not working on roboRIO

usb-dead.title: RIO does not answer over USB or Ethernet
steps: Try a different USB cable and a different laptop USB port. Make sure NI FRC Game Tools is installed so the driver exists.
Hold the reset button at least 5 seconds to enter Safe Mode, then try the Imaging Tool over USB.
Unshielded USB extensions have carried static that killed both RIO USB ports. Remove extensions and try the built-in ports.
Check the Status light. Flashing without pause means the unrecoverable branch of this guide.

steps.text: Does the RIO still not answer, even in Safe Mode?

comm-red.question: Is the Comm light solid red or blinking red?

no-code.title: Solid red Comm: DS connected, no user code running
steps: In the DS click Restart Robot Code and wait 15 seconds.
Read the DS Console. A stack trace at start means the code crashed. Fix that first.
Check the WPILib year of the code matches the RIO image year. A mismatch never runs.
Reboot the RIO. Redeploy from the team laptop if code still does not start.

steps.text: Is the Comm light still solid red?
steps.yes: Find the crash in the DS Console with the team.

estop.title: Blinking red Comm: E-stop is active
steps: An E-stop stays latched until it is cleared. The robot E-stop and the field E-stop are separate. This is almost always the robot's.
Off the field the robot E-stop is the DS space bar. On the field it is the team's own E-stop button on their driver station.

steps.text: Does the team have an E-stop button on their driver station?

steps: Clear it: reboot the roboRIO and restart the Driver Station software. Both hold a sticky E-stop.
Do both. A rebooted roboRIO that reconnects to a still-E-stopped DS drops straight back into E-stop.

steps.text: Does it E-stop again after both restart?
steps.yes: Find a stuck space bar or a joystick mapped to E-stop.

wont-move.title: Comm green, code running, robot will not move
steps: Check the Mode light. Off means disabled or brownout. Enable from the DS and watch it go green for teleop or orange for auto.
Check the RSL is on. A blinking RSL means enabled. No RSL means disabled or the RSL has no power.
Check the DS Joysticks light is green. Press F1 to rescan. Confirm the controller is in the slot the code expects.
Watch the battery voltage when enabling. A drop under 6.8 V disables outputs. Swap the battery.

steps.yes: Check the CAN bus with the CAN guide.
